AdminSla.firstResponseHint: How long the team has to send the first reply after a ticket is opened. Counted in working hours only.
AdminSla.resolutionHint: How long the team has to fully solve the ticket. This includes the first response time and counts working hours only.
AdminSla.warningHint: When this share of the time is used up, an early warning is sent so the ticket can be rescued before it breaches. Example: 80 means a warning at 80%.

calendars.title: Business calendars
calendars.help: A calendar holds the working days and hours of one country or site, its time zone and its public holidays. SLA clocks and reminders count time only inside the calendar that applies to the ticket.
calendars.name: Calendar name
calendars.recalcHelp: After you change working hours or holidays, open tickets keep their old deadlines until you recalculate them. This is recorded in the audit log.
calendars.deleteHelp: A calendar used by the SLA targets cannot be deleted. Organisations, branches and teams using it go back to the default.
calendars.assignHelp: A ticket follows the calendar of the customer's branch, then their organisation, then the team handling it, then the default calendar.

SlaReport.title: SLA report
SlaReport.subtitle: How well deadlines are being met for the tickets you can see.
SlaReport.atRiskEmpty: No ticket is breached or due soon.
SlaReport.note: Based on tickets created in the period. A ticket counts as met when it was answered or resolved before its deadline. Tickets closed as cancelled, duplicate or spam are not counted.
SlaReport.cyclesHelp: Every reopen starts a new SLA cycle. The first cycle is kept as it was, so a reopened ticket never hides a missed first deadline or double counts.

AdminCatalog.title: Categories and custom fields
AdminCatalog.subtitle: Manage the categories customers choose when they open a ticket, and the extra fields they fill in.
AdminCatalog.fieldsHint: A field can apply to all categories or to one. Staff-only fields are filled in by the support team on the ticket.
AdminCatalog.optionsHint: One option per line: value | English label | Arabic label. The Arabic label is optional.
AdminCatalog.fixedPriorityHint: New tickets get this priority automatically and staff cannot change it. A subcategory overrides its category.
AdminCatalog.isPrivateHint: Customers cannot see or choose a private category. Staff can still use it.
AdminCatalog.autoAssignHint: ON: new tickets go to the team member with the fewest open tickets (agents who have auto-assign switched on). OFF: tickets wait in the team queue.

AdminSettings.title: System settings
AdminSettings.subtitle: Settings that change how the system behaves.
AdminSettings.reopenHint: How long after a ticket is closed the customer can still reopen it.
AdminSettings.autoCloseHint: A resolved ticket closes by itself after this many days without a customer reply.
AdminSettings.emailHint: Turn this on only after the email provider key is configured on the server. Until then emails stay queued.
AdminSettings.note: Business hours, holidays and SLA targets are on the SLA settings page.
AdminSettings.regHelp: Who can create an account. Email confirmation is always required first.
AdminSettings.reg_closed_help: Nobody can register. The Create account option is removed everywhere. Branch and organization admins create the accounts.
AdminSettings.reg_approval_help: Customers create an account and confirm their email. An administrator then assigns the organization and approves.
AdminSettings.reg_pick_approval_help: Customers pick their organization and branch and confirm their email. The admins of that branch or organization approve, and are emailed.
AdminSettings.reg_pick_auto_help: Customers pick their organization and branch, confirm their email, and can sign in at once.
AdminSettings.regNote: Changing this does not affect accounts already waiting for approval.
AdminSettings.timersHelp: These timers run for tickets waiting on the customer and for resolved tickets. Days are calendar days.
AdminSettings.reminder1: First reminder to the customer (days after waiting starts)
AdminSettings.resolvedReminder: Reminder after a ticket is resolved (days)
AdminSettings.minReply: Minimum reply length to count as a first response (characters)
AdminSettings.timersHint: Use 0 to turn a step off. Reminders must come in order and before the automatic close. Changes apply from the next minute.
AdminSettings.captchaHelp: Adds a Cloudflare Turnstile check to the sign-up form so bots cannot create accounts. Create a free Turnstile widget in the Cloudflare dashboard and paste its two keys here.
AdminSettings.captchaRecommended: Recommended: the current mode activates accounts with no approval, so a captcha is the only bot filter.
AdminSettings.captchaClosed: Sign-up is closed, so the captcha has nothing to protect right now.
AdminSettings.captchaEnable: Require the captcha on the sign-up form
AdminSettings.captchaSecretSaved: A secret key is saved. Leave empty to keep it.
AdminSettings.captchaKeysHint: The site key is shown on the sign-up page. The secret key stays on the server and is never shown again. Cloudflare test keys: site key 1x00000000000000000000AA, secret key 1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA (always pass).
AdminSettings.pwHelp: Rules for every new password: sign-up, reset, change, and accounts created by administrators.
AdminSettings.pwApplies: Existing passwords keep working until they are changed.
AdminSettings.pwExpireHelp: When a password is older than the limit, the person must renew it at the next sign-in: we email a one-time code, then they choose a new password.
AdminSettings.pwWarnHint: Example: 7, 4 and 1 send warnings a week, four days and one day before the password expires. Use 0 to skip a warning. The wording is editable under Email templates ("Your password expires").
AdminSettings.captchaAlso: Also protects the forgot-password and email-code forms.
AdminSettings.autoRefreshHint: Ticket lists and ticket pages re-read their data every this many seconds while the page is open. Use 0 to turn it off, otherwise 10 to 3600.

generic.title: How to change the moves from this status
items: Staff: tick it to let support staff move the ticket there from the ticket page. Moves to Resolved and Closed also need the Resolve or Close permission on the person's account type.

Customer: tick it to give the customer a button for that move. Today customers have buttons only for confirming a resolved ticket (Resolved → Closed) and for reopening (Resolved or Closed → Reopened). Other customer ticks are saved but show no button.
Reason: tick it to make the person write a reason each time. The reason is kept in the ticket history and the audit log. It is greyed out until Staff or Customer is ticked.
Press Save at the bottom. Changes apply at once to every open ticket. The live diagram above shows the result before you save, and the safety check stops any change that would leave a ticket stuck.
generic.effectTitle: What this status does and what changes if you edit it

effects: A ticket is New until someone starts on it. The first real staff reply (20 characters or more) also moves it to In progress by itself, whatever this table says.
Moving to Open or In progress is how a team lead or agent picks up a ticket without replying yet.
Closed from New (with a reason) is the quick way to clear spam and duplicates. If you untick it, those tickets must first be moved to another status.
tips: Do not allow Pending customer here unless you want the SLA to pause before anyone has replied.
Do not remove every move from New. The safety check blocks it because tickets could never leave.

effects: Open means the ticket is ready or assigned and waits for an agent.
Pending customer pauses the SLA clock and starts the reminders to the customer (days 2, 4, 7, then close on day 10).
Resolved ends the SLA clock and asks for a resolution summary.
tips: A real staff reply moves Open to In progress by itself, so the manual move is mostly for taking ownership without replying.

effects: In progress is the main working status, and the SLA clock is running.
Open sends the ticket back to the waiting list (for example when it is returned to the team).
Pending customer and Pending internal pause the clock if the pause options are on for that priority (Administration → SLA).
Resolved stops the clock, needs a resolution summary and the Resolve permission, and starts the customer's waiting period.
tips: If you remove Resolved here, agents cannot finish tickets. The safety check will warn you.

effects: The clock is paused and the reminder timers run. If the customer replies, the ticket goes back to In progress by itself and the clock continues. This automatic move is not in the table.
Closed from here (with a reason) is the manual alternative to the automatic close on day 10 with the reason No customer response.
Any move out of this status resumes the clock.
tips: Leave the Customer column unticked. Customers return the ticket by replying, not with a button.
Making Reason required on Closed is a good habit, so the history explains why a ticket was closed early.

effects: Used while another team or a supplier works on it. Customers still see In progress, so they are not told about hand-offs.
The clock pauses only if the pause option for internal waiting is on in Administration → SLA.
There are no automatic reminders for this status, so keep a way back to In progress.
tips: If you add a move to Closed here, remember the agent also needs the Close permission.

effects: Staff have no moves from Resolved by default. The next step belongs to the customer: confirm (it closes as Resolved and confirmed), ask for more help (it reopens and starts a new SLA cycle), or just send a message.
If the customer does nothing, the ticket closes by itself after the waiting period (5 days by default, with a reminder on day 3). This automatic close is fixed and not part of this table.
Ticking Staff → Reopened lets agents reopen a resolved ticket on the customer's behalf.
tips: Unticking the customer moves removes the buttons from the customer's ticket page. Only do that if you want to handle confirmations yourself.
Change the waiting days and the reminder in Administration → General settings → System settings.

effects: Closed is final unless someone reopens it. Reopening starts a new SLA cycle and keeps the first one for reports.

Customer → Reopened is also limited by the reopen window (30 days by default) and by the closure reason. Tickets closed as Duplicate or Spam can never be reopened by the customer, whatever you tick here.
Unticking Customer → Reopened stops all customer reopening, and they can only create a follow-up ticket.
tips: Keep Reason required for Reopened so you always know why a closed ticket came back.
Staff → Reopened is useful when a customer calls instead of using the app.

effects: Reopened behaves like Open: a new SLA cycle has just started with fresh deadlines, and the first cycle is saved.
From here the ticket normally goes to In progress, or straight to Pending or Resolved.
tips: Keep at least one route to Resolved. The safety check requires it.

StatusGuide.title: Ticket lifecycle guide
StatusGuide.subtitle: Everything about how a ticket moves from New to Closed, how to change that, and how the service clocks (SLA) and calendars work. Written for administrators and team leaders.
StatusGuide.openHelp: Not sure what a setting does? The guide explains every status, timer, reason and SLA rule in plain language.

sections.title: 1. The big picture
sections.lead: A ticket is a customer's request for help. From the moment it is created until it is finished, it is always in exactly one status. This guide explains each status, who can move a ticket, what happens by itself, and how to change the rules safely.
bullets: The lifecycle: the statuses and the allowed moves between them (Administration → Ticket status).
The timers: reminders and automatic closing that run on their own (Administration → General settings → System settings).
The SLA: the promised response and resolution times, counted only in working hours (Administration → SLA).
sections.note: Every change you make on these screens is saved in the audit log with your name and the time, so nothing changes silently.

sections.title: 2. The eight statuses
sections.lead: The names below are the defaults. You can rename any of them, change the colour and the description; the behaviour stays the same.

head: Status
Customer sees
What it means
Service clock
rows: Just created. Nobody has started yet.
Ready or assigned, waiting for an agent to begin.
An agent is working on it and has replied to the customer.
We need an answer from the customer.
Waiting for another team or a third party. The customer is not told the difference.
The agent fixed it and wrote a resolution summary. It waits for the customer to confirm.
Finished. The reason it was closed is always recorded.
A resolved or closed ticket needs work again.

sections.note: Pending internal is shown to customers as In progress on purpose, so they do not see internal hand-offs.

sections.title: 3. A normal journey
steps: The customer creates a ticket. It starts as New.
An agent replies with a real answer (at least 20 characters). The ticket moves to In progress by itself and the first-response clock is met.
If the agent needs information, they set Pending customer. The service clock pauses and the reminder timers start.
When the customer replies, the ticket returns to In progress and the clock continues.
The agent sets Resolved and writes what was done. The customer is asked to confirm.
The customer confirms (the ticket closes as Resolved and confirmed), asks for more help (it reopens), or does nothing (it closes by itself after the waiting period).

sections.title: 4. Who can move a ticket, and to where
sections.lead: The allowed moves are a table you control. These are the defaults.
bullets: From New, staff can move a ticket to Open, In progress or Pending internal.
From Open or In progress, staff can move it to Pending customer, Pending internal, or Resolved (and between Open and In progress).
From Pending customer or Pending internal, staff can return it to In progress or mark it Resolved.
Moving to Resolved needs the Resolve permission.
From New or Pending customer, staff can close a ticket with a reason. This needs the Close permission.
Customers can confirm a Resolved ticket (it closes), or reopen a Resolved or Closed ticket with a reason.
Staff can reopen a Closed ticket with a reason.
sections.note: Automatic moves (closing a resolved ticket, closing when the customer never answers, starting an SLA cycle on reopen) are fixed. You can change their timing, but not switch the rules off.

sections.title: 5. How to change the lifecycle
sections.lead: Open Administration → Ticket status. You need the Manage settings permission.
steps: Open a status to change its names (staff and customer, English and Arabic), its colour, and its description. Save.
In the moves table, tick or untick a move for staff or for the customer. Mark a move as needing a reason if you want a written explanation each time.
Watch the live diagram: it redraws as you change the table so you can see the effect before you save.
Press Save. The system checks the flow first. If something is wrong it shows what, and nothing is saved.
To go back to the standard flow at any time, press Reset to default.
bullets: A status nobody can reach.
An active status with no route to Resolved for staff.
A status with no route to Closed.
Anything that would let a ticket get stuck.
sections.warn: Changes apply immediately to every open ticket. Make changes outside busy hours and test with a test ticket first.

sections.title: 6. Closure reasons
sections.lead: Closed is a status. The reason it was closed is stored separately, so reports can tell a solved ticket from a duplicate.

head: Reason
Who sets it
Customer can reopen?
rows: The system, after the waiting period
The system, after the last reminder
The system, when a cancellation is approved

steps: Open Administration → Ticket status → Closure reasons.
Add a reason, rename it in English and Arabic, and choose whether the customer may reopen.
Switch a reason off to hide it from staff. Existing tickets keep it.
Built-in reasons cannot be deleted because the automatic rules depend on them.
sections.note: Staff pick a reason every time they close a ticket. They cannot pick the three the system uses itself (resolved and confirmed, closed automatically, customer cancellation).

sections.title: 7. Permissions that matter here

head: Permission
What it allows
rows: Write replies and notes on a ticket.
Close a ticket with a reason, approve or reject cancellation requests, mark duplicates and spam.
Change everything in this guide: statuses, flow, closure reasons, timers, SLA, calendars.

steps: Open Administration → Permissions → Account types.
Choose the account type (for example Agent or Team leader).
Tick or untick Resolve and Close. Save.
sections.note: Giving Close only to team leaders is a common choice: agents resolve, leaders close and decide cancellations.

sections.title: 8. Automatic reminders and closing
sections.lead: These run every minute without anyone doing anything. All days are calendar days, counted in the time zone of the ticket's calendar, and messages go out when that calendar opens.

head: When
Day
What happens
rows: Final warning: the ticket will be closed soon
Closed automatically with the reason No customer response
Reminder: please confirm it is fixed or ask for more help
Closed automatically with the reason Closed automatically after resolution

steps: Open Administration → General settings → System settings.
Under Reminders and automatic closing, change the days. Use 0 to turn a step off.
Save. The new numbers apply from the next minute.
bullets: Reminders must stay in order and before the automatic close. The screen will not save an invalid order.
Each reminder is sent once per waiting period. If the customer answers and later the ticket waits again, the count starts again.
Customers receive reminders in the app and by email when email sending is on.

sections.title: 9. What the customer can do
bullets: Resolved ticket: choose It is solved (closes it), I still need help (reopens it with a reason), or Just send a message (adds a note and keeps it Resolved without restarting the timer).
Active ticket: cancel it. If no one has replied yet, it is cancelled straight away. If the team has started, the customer sends a request and can withdraw it while it waits.
Closed ticket: reopen it with a reason within the reopen window (30 days by default). Tickets closed as Duplicate or Spam cannot be reopened.
Closed ticket: create a follow-up ticket that links back to the old one.
sections.note: You can change the reopen window and the automatic closing days in System settings.

sections.title: 10. Cancellations, duplicates and spam (staff)
steps: Cancellation request: a card appears on the ticket. Write a note and press Approve and close, or Reject request (a note is required when rejecting and the customer is told).

Duplicate: on the second ticket, enter the reference of the original (for example CTS-2026-000123) and press Close as duplicate. The two tickets are linked, and the customer sees which ticket replaced theirs.
Spam: press Mark as spam and confirm. The ticket closes and the customer cannot reopen it.
sections.note: These actions need the Close permission. They also finish the SLA so the ticket never counts as a missed deadline.

sections.title: 11. SLA: the promised times
sections.lead: The SLA has two clocks for every ticket: first response and resolution. Both count working time only, using the calendar that applies to the ticket.
bullets: These targets are provisional and need business approval. Change them in Administration → SLA.
A reply counts as the first response only if it is a real answer from staff (at least 20 characters). A short Thanks does not stop the clock. You can change the length in System settings.
The clocks pause while the ticket is Pending customer or Pending internal, if the pause options for that priority are on.
A warning goes to staff when the set percentage of time is used, and a breach alert when the deadline passes. Who is told is set per priority.
Changing targets affects new tickets and tickets whose priority changes. Open tickets keep their deadlines until you recalculate.

sections.title: 12. Reopened tickets and SLA cycles
paras: When a ticket is reopened, a new SLA cycle starts with fresh deadlines from that moment. The first cycle is saved exactly as it ended.
bullets: A ticket that missed its first deadline stays counted as missed, even if the reopen cycle goes well.
Reports show original handling and after-reopen handling separately.
The countdown on the ticket always shows the current cycle.

sections.title: 13. Business calendars
sections.lead: A calendar is the working days and hours of a country or site, its time zone and its public holidays. Two are included: Egypt (Sunday to Thursday, 09:00 to 17:00) and South Africa (Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00).
steps: Open Administration → SLA → Business calendars.
Open a calendar to change its working days and hours, its time zone, or its name.
Add holidays one by one. Fixed-date holidays are included for 2026 and 2027; moving holidays such as Eid must be added each year.
Choose the default calendar for the SLA targets.
Under Which calendar applies, give an organisation, branch or team its own calendar.
paras: A ticket follows the first calendar it finds in this order:
bullets: The customer's branch
The customer's organisation
The team handling the ticket
The default calendar
sections.warn: After changing hours or holidays, press Recalculate open tickets on that calendar. Otherwise open tickets keep their old deadlines. Each recalculation is written to the audit log.

sections.title: 14. Reports
bullets: The SLA report shows the percentage met for first response and resolution, split into original handling and after reopen.
Tickets closed as cancelled, duplicate or spam are not counted in the SLA report.
In the other reports, a ticket that missed a deadline in an earlier cycle is not counted as met.

sections.title: 15. Changing things safely
steps: Decide what you want to change and why. Write it down.
Make the change outside busy hours.
Test with a test ticket: create it as a customer, move it through the statuses, and check the customer's view.
Check the audit log to confirm what was saved.
Tell the team what changed.
If something looks wrong, use Reset to default for the flow, or set the old value back for timers and SLA.
sections.note: Test accounts and demo data should be removed before go-live so they do not appear in reports.

faq.a: The safety check found a problem and shows it above the table. Usually a status became unreachable or an active status cannot reach Resolved. Undo that move and save again.

faq.q: An agent cannot resolve or close a ticket.
faq.a: They need the Resolve or Close permission. Add it to their account type. Also check that the move exists in the flow table for staff.

faq.q: A customer did not get a reminder.
faq.a: Check that the ticket is Pending customer or Resolved, that the reminder day has been reached, that the step is not set to 0, and that email sending is on in System settings.
Look at its closure reason. No customer response means the last reminder passed. Closed automatically after resolution means the customer did not answer within the waiting period.

faq.q: A customer cannot reopen a ticket.
faq.a: The ticket was closed as Duplicate or Spam, or the reopen window has passed. They can create a follow-up ticket instead.
Check the calendar that applies to the customer's branch, organisation and team, the time zone, and the holidays. Then recalculate open tickets.

faq.q: I renamed a status. Do old tickets change?
faq.a: Yes, the name changes everywhere, in the app, in emails and in reports. The status itself and its behaviour stay the same.

head: Term
Meaning
rows: Service level agreement: the response and resolution times we promise.
The first real answer from staff to the customer.
The time from creation to Resolved.
A deadline passed without the step being done.
Time inside the calendar's working hours, excluding days off and holidays.
One run of the SLA clocks. A reopen starts a new cycle.
Any day on the calendar, including days off. Reminder timers use these.
The permanent record of who changed what and when.
